note: The sources mention cordyceps only in passing (rice media, dim early incubation, fast fruiting in high-exchange bags, stalled white heads). The rest of this drawing is general knowledge, not from the sources.

stages.a: Rice grains packed in a filter bag.
stages.v: Some cordyceps growers dry-bag rice-based media with a Fenrir-type filler.

stages.a: White mycelium knits the rice into one mat.
stages.v: Early incubation goes best in dim light or none; black bags help.

stages.a: Small pins rise from the mat.
stages.v: Fast species like cordyceps may suit fruiting inside high-exchange (B patch) bags.

stages.a: Slender clubs stretch up; their tops swell into the fertile heads.
Full-height clubs with swollen, pimpled heads.
stages.v: It degenerates quickly, especially through serial liquid-culture expansion. Preserve good cultures early.

labels.a: A closed bag with a filter patch.
labels.v: Fast species like cordyceps may suit high-exchange (B patch) bags.

labels.a: The rice the culture grows on.
A white mat over the rice.
The swollen top, pimpled with tiny bumps where the spores form.
A short, fat white head that stopped growing.
labels.v: Stalled white heads that look like stroma also show up with cordyceps.
